## Findings

### 1. Inline Prose Emphasis Idiom Catalog

The site uses a **four-tier emphasis system**, applied against body prose that is deliberately dimmed to `var(--text-secondary)` (#b0bcc8). Emphasis works by *brightening*, not coloring, in most cases.

| Tier | Markup | CSS | Frequency observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Standard emphasis | plain `<strong>` | `.doc-content strong { color: var(--text); font-weight: 600; }` (learn-understanding.html:467); anatomy equivalent `.intro-body strong { color: var(--text); }` (daaf_anatomy.css:532) | 147 instances across 147 `<p>` in learn-understanding — **averaging ~1 per paragraph**, often the paragraph's thesis phrase |
| 2. Accent emphasis (rare, "headline claims") | `<strong style="color: var(--accent);">` inline style, no class | teal #22d3a8 over the default strong rules | Only **8** instances in the entire anatomy page (index.html:164,168,171,220,222), **1** in product index vs 63 plain strongs. Reserved for value-proposition payoffs: "~30 minutes of raw human time", "speed and flexibility without sacrificing accountability and rigor" |
| 3. De-emphasis italic | `<em>` | `.doc-content em { color: var(--text-muted); font-style: italic; }` (learn-understanding.html:468) — note em is *dimmer* than body text | 18 instances; single-word stress: "*why*", "*everyone*" |
| 4. Technical tokens | `<code>` | `font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.85em; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.06); padding: 0.15em 0.4em; border-radius: 4px; color: var(--accent-mint);` (learn-understanding.html:472-479) | 79 instances — mint #6ee7b7 for filenames, commands, variables |

**Gradient text is heading-only**: `.gradient-text { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #22d3a8 0%, #6ee7b7 50%, #6366f1 100%); -webkit-background-clip: text; -webkit-text-fill-color: transparent; background-clip: text; }` (learn-understanding.html:105-110; identical at daaf_anatomy.css:508-513). Used only inside `<h1>`/`<h2>` spans (e.g., anatomy index.html:127, 208), never in body prose. 5 uses on the product homepage.

**Replication rule for the viewer:** keep body copy at `--text-secondary`; bold one thesis phrase per paragraph with plain `<strong>` (white, w600); use teal accent-strong at most once per major section for a number/claim the reader must retain; use mint `<code>` for model names/metric identifiers; reserve gradient spans for the h1.

### 3. Learn-Page TOC ("On this page") Recipe

**Layout container** (learn-understanding.html:384-392):
```css
:root { --toc-width: 220px; --toc-scroll-height: 0px; }
.doc-layout {
    max-width: var(--content-max);  /* 1100px */
    margin: 0 auto;
    padding: clamp(2rem, 4vw, 3rem) clamp(1.5rem, 5vw, 3rem) clamp(4rem, 8vw, 6rem);
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: var(--toc-width) 1fr;
    gap: clamp(2rem, 4vw, 3.5rem);
    overflow-x: clip;
}
```

**Mobile CSS, verbatim — breakpoint `@media (max-width: 960px)`** (lines 942-1007). Desktop default is `.toc-mobile-wrap { display: none; }` (line 436):
```css
@media (max-width: 960px) {
    :root { --toc-scroll-height: 50px; }       /* feeds scroll-padding-top */
    .doc-layout { grid-template-columns: 1fr; padding: 2rem 1.5rem 4rem; }
    .doc-toc { display: none; }
    .toc-mobile-wrap {
        display: block;
        position: sticky;
        top: calc(var(--nav-height) + 3px);     /* below nav + gradient strip */
        z-index: 50;
        background: rgba(10, 15, 28, 0.92);
        backdrop-filter: blur(10px);
        -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(10px);
        border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
    }
    /* edge-fade affordances */
    .toc-mobile-wrap::before, .toc-mobile-wrap::after {
        content: ''; position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0;
        width: 3rem; z-index: 2; pointer-events: none;
    }
    .toc-mobile-wrap::before { left: 0;  background: linear-gradient(to right, rgba(10,15,28,0.92), transparent); }
    .toc-mobile-wrap::after  { right: 0; background: linear-gradient(to left,  rgba(10,15,28,0.92), transparent); }
    .toc-mobile {
        display: block; padding: 0.25rem 0;
        overflow-x: auto;
        scrollbar-width: none; -ms-overflow-style: none;
    }
    .toc-mobile::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
    .toc-mobile-inner { display: flex; gap: 0.75rem; padding: 0 1.25rem; width: max-content; }
    .toc-mobile a {
        font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 400;
        color: var(--text-muted); padding: 0.75rem 0.65rem;
        white-space: nowrap; transition: color 0.2s;
    }
    .toc-mobile a:hover { color: var(--text-secondary); opacity: 1; }
    .toc-mobile a.toc-active { color: var(--accent); }
}
```

**Anchor offset trick** (line 74): `html { scroll-behavior: smooth; scroll-padding-top: calc(var(--nav-height) + 3px + var(--toc-scroll-height) + 0.5rem); }` — `--toc-scroll-height` is 0 on desktop, 50px under 960px, so anchors land below the sticky mobile TOC bar.

**Scrollspy JS, verbatim** (lines 2019-2066) — one IntersectionObserver drives both TOCs and auto-centers the mobile bar:
```js
(function() {
    var sidebarLinks = document.querySelectorAll('.doc-toc a');
    var mobileLinks = document.querySelectorAll('.toc-mobile a');
    var allLinks = Array.from(sidebarLinks).concat(Array.from(mobileLinks));
    var sections = [];
    sidebarLinks.forEach(function(link) {
        var id = link.getAttribute('href').substring(1);
        var el = document.getElementById(id);
        if (el) sections.push(el);
    });
    if (!sections.length) return;
    var mobileScrollTimer = null;
    var clickLockUntil = 0;
    var observer = new IntersectionObserver(function(entries) {
        entries.forEach(function(entry) {
            if (entry.isIntersecting) {
                var id = entry.target.id;
                allLinks.forEach(function(link) {
                    link.classList.toggle('toc-active', link.getAttribute('href') === '#' + id);
                });
                if (Date.now() < clickLockUntil) return;
                clearTimeout(mobileScrollTimer);
                mobileScrollTimer = setTimeout(function() {
                    var activeMobile = document.querySelector('.toc-mobile a.toc-active');
                    if (activeMobile) {
                        var container = document.getElementById('toc-mobile');
                        var scrollLeft = activeMobile.offsetLeft - container.offsetWidth / 2 + activeMobile.offsetWidth / 2;
                        container.scrollTo({ left: scrollLeft, behavior: 'smooth' });
                    }
                }, 600);
            }
        });
    }, { threshold: 0.1, rootMargin: '-90px 0px -55% 0px' });
    sections.forEach(function(el) { observer.observe(el); });
    allLinks.forEach(function(link) {
        link.addEventListener('click', function() { clickLockUntil = Date.now() + 1200; });
    });
})();
```
Behavior notes: observes the `h2[id]` section headings themselves (sections are heading elements, not wrappers); `rootMargin: '-90px 0px -55% 0px'` makes a heading "active" when it sits between the nav and the upper 45% of the viewport; a 600ms debounce + 1200ms click-lock prevent the mobile bar from jittering during smooth-scrolls.

### 4. Mobile Overflow-Prevention Techniques

All observed in learn-understanding.html unless noted:
1. **Global border-box reset**: `*, *::before, *::after { margin:0; padding:0; box-sizing: border-box; }` (line 41; daaf_anatomy.css:7).
2. **Body-level clamp**: `body { overflow-x: hidden; }` (line 82; daaf_anatomy.css:81).
3. **Layout-level clip**: `.doc-layout { overflow-x: clip; }` (line 391) — `clip` rather than `hidden` so `position: sticky` inside still works.
4. **Grid-child width discipline**: `.doc-content { max-width: 100%; overflow-wrap: break-word; word-break: break-word; min-width: 0; }` (line 442). The `min-width: 0` defeats the grid default `min-width: auto` that lets wide tables/code stretch the column — this is the most likely fix for the viewer's "left-right play". Same combo on anatomy's `.left-column` (daaf_anatomy.css:467). All grid panels also get `min-width: 0` (e.g., `.predict-panel`, line 720).
5. **Scroll containers for wide content, not page scroll**: `.doc-table-wrap { overflow-x: auto; margin: 1.25rem 0 1.5rem; -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; }` with `.doc-table { min-width: 480px; }` (lines 515-526); `.code-block { overflow-x: auto; white-space: pre; }` (lines 557-569).
6. **Edge-bleed at 560px**: `.doc-table-wrap { margin-left: -0.75rem; margin-right: -0.75rem; }` (line 1083) — tables bleed to viewport edge on phones so the scrollable region uses full width.
7. **Mobile TOC contains its own overflow**: `width: max-content` lives on the *inner* flex row (line 989) inside an `overflow-x: auto` scroller, so it never widens the page.
8. **Standard viewport meta**: `width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0` (line 13). No `100vw` widths anywhere (avoids scrollbar-width overflow).

### 5. Other Reusable Design-Language Observations

- **Section h2 dividers** (lines 443-453): `.doc-content h2 { font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 2rem); font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.02em; margin-top: 3rem; margin-bottom: 1.25rem; padding-top: 1.5rem; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }` with `h2:first-child` resetting all three. Gives a quiet ruled rhythm well-suited to benchmark sections. At 560px: `clamp(1.25rem, 5vw, 1.5rem)` (line 1080).
- **Data table idiom** (lines 527-554) — directly applicable to benchmark tables: `th { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--accent); text-align: left; padding: 0.65rem 1rem; border-bottom: 2px solid rgba(34,211,168,0.2); white-space: nowrap; }`; `td { padding: 0.6rem 1rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); color: var(--text-secondary); vertical-align: top; }`; `td strong { color: var(--text); }`; `tr:last-child td { border-bottom: none; }`; table `font-size: 0.85rem; line-height: 1.5;`.
- **Callout family** (lines 482-512): `.callout { border-left: 3px solid var(--accent); background: rgba(34,211,168,0.04); padding: 1.25rem 1.5rem; border-radius: 0 8px 8px 0; margin: 1.5rem 0; }` with modifiers `--note` (indigo), `--important` (#f59e0b amber), `--takeaway` (mint, plus an uppercase `.callout-label`). Useful for methodology caveats on the benchmark page.
- **3px brand strip**: `body::before { position: fixed; top:0; left:0; right:0; height:3px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--accent), var(--accent-mint), var(--accent-indigo)); z-index: 200; }` (lines 86-93) and nav sits at `top: 3px`.
- **Reveal-on-scroll** (lines 130-140, JS 1957-1972): `.reveal { opacity:0; transform: translateY(24px); transition: 0.7s var(--ease-out-expo); }` + `.revealed`, staggered `.reveal-d1`–`d5` (0.08s steps), IntersectionObserver `{ threshold: 0.08, rootMargin: '0px 0px -40px 0px' }`, with `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback (lines 1088-1096).
- **Shared easing token**: `--ease-out-expo: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` used on every hover/transition.
- **Accent callout box for key numbers** (daaf_anatomy.css:682-706): `.intro-impact` with 4px accent left-bar and `strong { font-family: var(--font-mono); color: var(--accent); }` — a good pattern for the battery-cost headline figure.

## Gaps and Limitations
- The anatomy hero has **no subtitle/date element** — its `.intro-subtitle` rule exists (daaf_anatomy.css:515-521) but the markup uses `.intro-body` divs instead; for a date line, the Learn page's `.breadcrumb` mono treatment is the closest site idiom.
- `daaf_anatomy.js` (3980 lines) was not read in depth; the anatomy page's nav/scroll behaviors beyond what HTML comments document were out of scope since the TOC ask targets the Learn page.
- `get-started.html` and the open-augments pages were not read; the two requested analogue pages covered all asks. If they use a different emphasis idiom it is uncaptured (LOW likelihood — tokens and nav markup are identical across pages read).
- Frequency counts are grep-based on tag patterns; multiline `<strong ...>` spanning attributes would be missed (none observed in samples).
